pr_title: Fix EVP aead interface for bench-marking ccm, gcm, ocb, and siv, where decryption fails
pr_body:
Fixed the bench-marking for the evp aead interface for ccm, gcm, ocb, and siv, where decryption fails when executing `openssl speed -evp aes-128-ccm -decrypt` and `openssl speed -evp aes-128-gcm -decrypt`. Related issues are [24686](https://github.com/openssl/openssl/issues/24686) and [24250](https://github.com/openssl/openssl/issues/24250). Now both encryption and decryption, with or without AAD, executes correctly without issues.ad

Additionally, previously there were the following two functions that handled both encryption and decryption. The first one only handled CCM. However, it was now changed to handle encryption of all AEAD which includes CCM, GCM, OCB, SIV. The other function was changed to handle decryption of AEAD modes.
1- `EVP_Update_loop_ccm()` -> `EVP_Update_loop_aead_enc()`
2- EVP_Update_loop_aead()` -> `EVP_Update_loop_aead_dec()`

This PR is a replica of the previously closed  PR #25809

issue_context.title: "Error finalizing cipher loop" when running openssl speed -evp -decrypt for AES-GCM
issue_context.body:
While running speed decrypt for aes-gcm in openssl3.2 getting Error finalizing cipher loop error.

![image](https://github.com/openssl/openssl/assets/138493920/73617190-6f91-404b-a7ea-03e6e4debeb7)

Note: Similar issue seen in https://github.com/openssl/openssl/issues/23657 and they mentioned that fix was available in https://github.com/openssl/openssl/pull/23757 and it got merged into master branch. But still seeing an issue with master branch for aes-gcm

![image](https://github.com/openssl/openssl/assets/138493920/18d2b811-9400-4811-864f-fe366fb48c87)
comments: @tom-cosgrove-arm can you comment on the fix you made in #23757?  I'm having trouble seeing how a fake tag can be used with aes in ccm or gcm mode?  I think it makes sense in aead mode because (again I think) the tag is validated independently of the decrypt operation, but in ccm mode the tag is never checked in the decrypt operation.  Its only checked in gcm mode, and I can't see how an arbitrary tag will pass that check.  It seems like instead for gcm mode, we should do an initial encryption of a buffer to obtain a tag and use that computed value consistently during the decrypt operation

> It seems like instead for gcm mode, we should do an initial encryption of a buffer to obtain a tag and use that computed value consistently during the decrypt operation

That would definitely be the best option

@ravulapx it seems like the consensus here is that the appropriate fix is, for gcm mode speed tests:

- [ ] Modify the speed_main function such that, when loopfunction is set to EVP_Update_loop, and -decrypt is selected, that we preform an initial encryption of a data buffer, and extract the tag from that result
- [ ] Modify EVP_Update_loop such that if a tag is assigned in speed_main, we use that as the input tag for decryption

that should avoid this problem.  Unfortunately I don't know when we are going to be able to get to this.  Would you be willing to create a PR for this effort?
@tom-cosgrove-arm your solution would certainly work.  I guess the question is "is it ok for us to test algorithm speed on failing inputs"?  If so, that would be a faster solution

@nhorman In general when I've written tests like this for other systems, I've gone in the direction you state (perform a genuine encryption and use that to test decryption performance). However, OpenSSL hasn't done that, so we are purely testing performance here, not correctness (which is why my original fix here, that didn't quite fix it). Since the algorithms we are testing always perform the decryption and tag computations, and only diverge in behaviour when checking the tag at the very last step, performance is still representative. We might want a note to that effect, either as a comment in the code or "elsewhere" (but I not sure where that else might be!)
@ravulapx are you interested in attempting to write a patch for this and submit it as a pull request, guided by the conversation above?

> @ravulapx are you interested in attempting to write a patch for this and submit it as a pull request, guided by the conversation above?

Hi @nhorman @tom-cosgrove-arm  @ravulapx, I opened a [PR](https://github.com/openssl/openssl/pull/25823) to get CCM and GCM through decryption successfully. As far as I believe, CCM, GCM, and OCB require a valid tag which is only computed after encrypting a message. 
For this reason, I made some modifications to the code in `speed.c` to encrypt the data first, get the tag, and then use it to decrypt. I haven't taken chacha into account but I tested both encryption and decryption, with and without AAD, using CCM, GCM, OCB, SIV, and GCM-SIV. The PR hasn't been merged yet, so let's see how that goes.
Fixed on all the branches thanks to @zelda923

review_comments:
This is a speed testing loop. Although in principle I agree with the "single responsibility principle", we should not take it fundamentally. I would not do this change. You could add more comments though to make the individual EVP API calls more clear. 

Also using thisNotationForFunctionNames would be wrong and not aligned with the OpenSSL code style.

Same comment here as well.

Reading long functions can be quite challenging. It's best to keep functions as small as possible, adhering to the single responsibility and clean code principle. This not only aids in quick understanding but also makes maintenance easier.

@shahsb Thanks a million for the feedback. I agree with all proposed changes. In fact, I was working on refactoring the code and adding support for chacha as well, but the intention was to create another PR as this one has been approved. What do you think?

Now that this PR is ready to merge, please don't make further changes to it. Any further changes are best addressed in a follow-on PR. If you want to refactor, maybe do that as one PR, before fixing ChaCha in a subsequent PR (smaller, more focussed PRs are easier and quicker to review - a query on one aspect doesn't hold up something that is only tangentially related)

Yes, I agree with addressing this as part of separate PRs. 

Also, I 100% agree on the fact that smaller & focused PRs are easier & quick to review. @tom-cosgrove-arm  - Thanks, Good point!
